title: Rusty review pass 4: jmap-client
notes:
Section: ownership/borrowing — CLEAN. All clones are necessary; no gratuitous allocation. No String-param-when-&str-would-do in production API (JmapRequestBuilder::new takes &[&str], auth constructors take &str).
Section: unsafe — CLEAN. #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at crate root. No unsafe anywhere.
Section: iterators/collections — CLEAN. No for-push loops that should be collect, no index loops, no len()==0, no .get(0). compute_sha256_hex uses fold correctly.
Section: lifetime annotations — CLEAN. No unnecessary explicit lifetimes; elision used correctly throughout.
Section: macros — CLEAN. No public-API macros. Standard derives only.
Section: clippy/language idioms — CLEAN except items covered by JMAP-o0i.1. No return-as-last-statement, no match-on-bool, no .len()==0, no .get(0)/.get(n-1), no String::from(''), no vec push in loop.
Section: traits — Findings filed as JMAP-o0i.2 and JMAP-o0i.3 (missing PartialEq derives on public types). No missing Display (ClientError has thiserror Display, all public error types display). No missing From impls — conversions are covered by #[from] in thiserror. No missing AsRef. No manual impls that should be derived (Debug on BearerAuth/BasicAuth is intentionally manual to redact credentials).
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — auth, blob, SSE, WS, and request builder code is idiomatic. Two structural gaps: (1) deserialization errors lose structure vs serialization errors (Parse/String asymmetry), (2) three clusters of public types missing PartialEq derives.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-o0i.3 (Session/AccountInfo PartialEq — serde_json::Value PartialEq but not Eq, so Eq cannot be derived; issue text notes this). Uncertainty driven by: did not run clippy locally to mechanically verify no additional clippy lints; reviewed by reading only.
